Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.securitycenter

Class SecurityProbe

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.securitycenter.SecurityProbe
public final class SecurityProbe extends Object
The AWT-free host-security seam for the Security Overview. It builds the command lines that probe the machine's mandatory-access-control and firewall posture and parses their output into small enums, so the whole table is unit-testable headless. Like AntivirusBackend, nothing here starts a process; SecurityCenterPanel runs the (fast) commands on a background thread only when the user opens or refreshes the overview.

SELinux is read with getenforce (Enforcing / Permissive / Disabled). The firewall is read with firewall-cmd --state; that call needs PolicyKit authorization, so on a session without it the probe reports SecurityProbe.FirewallState.UNKNOWN rather than guessing. A missing tool is reported by the panel as ABSENT, never as a silent "secure".

    • parseFirewallState

      public static SecurityProbe.FirewallState parseFirewallState(int exitCode, String output)
      Parses firewall-cmd --state. The command prints running or not running and exits non-zero when the daemon is down or the call is not authorized; an authorization denial is reported as SecurityProbe.FirewallState.UNKNOWN, not as "not running".
      Parameters:
      exitCode - the process exit code
      output - the trimmed command output (may be null / blank)
      Returns:
      the firewall state

    • describeVpn

      public static String describeVpn(boolean connected, boolean killSwitch)
      A short human label for the read-only VPN tunnel state, for the overview card. A connected tunnel is annotated with whether its kill switch is armed, since a tunnel that can silently fall back to clearnet is weaker than one that fails closed.
      Parameters:
      connected - whether a VPN tunnel is currently up
      killSwitch - whether the connected tunnel's kill switch is armed
      Returns:
      the display label, never null
